svg.title: Cell–cell interactions in cardiac fibrosis
svg.desc: A 16:9 circular evidence synthesis of 141 interaction findings from 33 papers. Four cell compartments surround a chord network of signals (colour = sender; solid = functional evidence; dashed = computational prediction; bar ends = inhibition). Side cards summarise each compartment; numbered badges link to the papers.

svg.text: How cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts, endothelial cells and macrophages signal to one another in injury and repair

g.title: Resident CCR2- / TIM4+ macrophages: restrain fibrosis, support coronary growth, clear cardiomyocyte exophers. Refs: 17, 18, 19
Monocyte-derived CCR2+ and SPP1+ macrophages: pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic; express SPP1, THBS1, FN1. Refs: 3, 15, 16, 17
Pericardial GATA6+ and human FN1+ macrophages: anti-fibrotic (CST3), relocate to the infarct. Refs: 13, 14, 20
Quiescent / SCARA5+ fibroblasts with an HTRA3-high, innate-immunity module. Refs: 3, 6
Activated POSTN+, Cilp+/Thbs4+ and ECM-Fib states: dominant matrix producers. Refs: 2, 8, 23
αSMA+ myofibroblasts: RUNX1, Yap/Taz–TEAD and an autocrine TIMP1 loop sustain them. Refs: 3, 7, 10
Injured cardiomyocytes induce ZEB2 (pro-angiogenic) and NOX4 (inflammasome-driving). Refs: 27, 28
p16+ senescent cardiomyocytes after ischaemia–reperfusion; secrete IL-6. Refs: 26
Cardiomyocytes eject mitochondria-laden exophers that resident macrophages clear via MERTK. Refs: 19
Vascular ECs: capillary loss and rarefaction after MI; broad signalling gains in human heart failure. Refs: 1, 2, 22
Immunomodulatory ECs (CD45+ ERG+, MHC-II+): emerge day 1 after MI. Refs: 21
Lymphatic ECs: VEGF-C/VEGFR3-driven lymphangiogenesis clears immune cells via LYVE-1. Refs: 29, 30
Cardiac fibrosis: the shared output of the interaction network.
Macrophages & monocytes → Fibroblasts: CCL24 · HB-EGF · miR-21 (stimulatory; functional / experimental evidence). Refs: 11, 12, 16
Macrophages & monocytes → Fibroblasts: CST3 (inhibitory; functional / experimental evidence). Refs: 13
Fibroblasts → Macrophages & monocytes: IL-33 · secretome (stimulatory; functional / experimental evidence). Refs: 7
Cardiomyocytes → Fibroblasts: EV miR-24-3p (inhibitory; functional / experimental evidence). Refs: 25
Cardiomyocytes → Fibroblasts: TGF-β1 · IL-6 (stimulatory; functional / experimental evidence). Refs: 5, 26
Fibroblasts → Cardiomyocytes: TGF-β · stiffness (stimulatory; functional / experimental evidence). Refs: 6, 32, 33
Cardiomyocytes → Macrophages & monocytes: Exophers → MERTK (stimulatory; functional / experimental evidence). Refs: 19
Macrophages & monocytes → Cardiomyocytes: FAK contact · CX43 (stimulatory; functional / experimental evidence). Refs: 18, 31
Cardiomyocytes → Endothelial cells: ZEB2 → TMSB4/PTMA (stimulatory; functional / experimental evidence). Refs: 28
Macrophages & monocytes → Endothelial cells: VEGF-A · IGF1 · VEGF-C (stimulatory; functional / experimental evidence). Refs: 17, 18, 29
Fibroblasts → Endothelial cells: exo-miR-200a-3p (inhibitory; functional / experimental evidence). Refs: 24
Endothelial cells → Macrophages & monocytes: Lymphatic clearance (stimulatory; functional / experimental evidence). Refs: 30
Endothelial cells → Fibroblasts: Laminin · collagen (stimulatory; computational prediction). Refs: 1

g.title:
CCL24→CCR3 and HB-EGF→EGFR activate fibroblasts
CF038-INT-F01 (Cardiac resident macrophages → source of CCL24): Resident macrophages were the dominant Ccl24-expressing cells; Ccl24 transcripts were seen in macrophages but not fibroblasts or cardiomyocytes, expression was exclusive to resident macrophages in sham and TAC hearts, about 70% of resident macrophages were CCL24-lineage positive with no other cell type labelled, cardiac CCL24 protein doubled within 1 week of TAC and returned to baseline at 4 weeks, and chimeras whose myeloid compartment was replaced by monocyte-derived macrophages had almost no cardiac CCL24 [Evidence: Observational with genetic reporter and chimera-based source attribution]
CF038-INT-F02 (IL-4 and IL-10 (cardiac milieu) → resident macrophages (CCL24 output)): TAC increased cardiac IL-4 and IL-10 at 1 week; combined IL-4 and IL-10 stimulated substantial CCL24 production by sorted macrophages, while either cytokine alone failed to do so, and resident macrophages expressed higher IL-4 receptor than monocyte-derived macrophages [Evidence: Functional perturbation (exogenous cytokine addition, ex vivo)]
CF038-INT-F03 (Macrophage-derived CCL24 → myocardium (fibrosis and function)): CCL24 knockout mice showed improved ejection fraction and fractional shortening at 1, 2 and 4 weeks after TAC with no baseline or sham differences and no difference in pressure gradient; they had transiently increased heart/body weight ratio and cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area at 1 week that normalised by 4 weeks. Collagen formation, collagen biosynthesis and ECM organization gene sets were downregulated, with reduced Tgfb2, Col5a1, Postn, Col14a1, Mmp2 and reduced Col1, Acta2, Mmp2, Tgfβ by qPCR, about 40% less fibrotic area, and fewer αSMA+vimentin+ myofibroblasts. CCL24 neutralizing antibody reproduced the functional improvement; chimeras reconstituted with CCL24-knockout monocyte-derived macrophages showed no improvement [Evidence: Functional perturbation (global genetic deletion plus antibody blockade)]
CF038-INT-F04 (CCL24 (macrophage-derived in vivo) → cardiac fibroblasts): CCR3 was most highly expressed on cardiac fibroblasts and increased with TAC. Recombinant CCL24 increased fibroblast number and Ki67+ fraction, increased αSMA+ myofibroblasts, and increased fibroblast-derived TGF-β in the supernatant; it induced periostin by 24 h and collagen I and αSMA by 48 h. CCR3 blockade abolished all three responses, whereas TGF-β blockade prevented the periostin and αSMA increases but not collagen I. The TAC-induced CCR3 ligands CCL2, CCL7 and CCL8 did not increase αSMA. PI3K inhibition reversed CCL24-induced αSMA and blocked Akt phosphorylation, while a PI3K activator induced αSMA independently of CCL24 and still acted in CCR3-knockdown fibroblasts, which failed to respond to CCL24 [Evidence: Functional perturbation (recombinant ligand, receptor and ligand blockade, pathway inhibition, genetic knockdown)]
CF038-INT-F05 (Fibroblast CCR3 → fibrosis and cardiac function (receiver-side requirement)): Fibroblast-restricted CCR3 knockdown improved ejection fraction and fractional shortening after TAC, reduced Timp1 with trends for Col1, Col3 and Tgfβ1, and reduced collagen deposition, fibrotic area and αSMA+vimentin+ myofibroblast area, without changes in heart/body or lung/body weight or chamber dimensions. The CCR3 antagonist likewise improved function and reduced interstitial fibrosis. Separately, CCL24 deficiency did not prevent TAC-induced expansion of cardiac T, NK, B, neutrophil, eosinophil or total macrophage populations and did not change inflammatory gene expression, and the CCR3 antagonist did not alter immune cell proportions apart from a mild decrease in total macrophage number [Evidence: Functional perturbation (conditional receptor deletion and pharmacological antagonism) with important negative immune results]
CF041-INT-F01 (DNMT3A CHIP monocytes → cardiac fibroblasts (and other cardiac cell types)): Monocytes from DNMT3A CHIP carriers showed the highest number of predicted outgoing signals to cardiac fibroblasts and more predicted interactions than non-carrier monocytes with most cell types, in both healthy and HFrEF cardiac tissue; the largest CHIP-enriched set was monocyte-to-fibroblast in HFrEF samples, with EGF, RESISTIN and IGF common to both tissue contexts and EGFR downstream pathways (phospholipase C-gamma, GRB2, SHC1) enriched [Evidence: Computational prediction (on reused external datasets; flagged)]
CF041-INT-F02 (DNMT3A-silenced monocytes → cardiac fibroblasts; → cardiospheres): Supernatant from DNMT3A-silenced monocytes increased fibroblast ACTA2 at mRNA and protein level, increased TGFB1 expression, stimulated contraction and migration, augmented collagen expression and produced a non-significant trend to increased proliferation. In cardiospheres it reduced beating frequency without changing sphere size, increased PDGFRα+ area and increased αSMA; no cytotoxic effect was seen on the cardiomyocyte line [Evidence: Functional perturbation (gene silencing plus conditioned-medium transfer)]
CF041-INT-F03 (Monocyte-derived HB-EGF → cardiac fibroblasts): HBEGF and AREG were significantly higher in circulating monocytes of DNMT3A CHIP carriers and EGFR was the highest-expressed EGF receptor family member in cardiac fibroblasts; plasma HB-EGF was elevated in CHIP carriers, and DNMT3A silencing increased HB-EGF mRNA and protein and the sheddases ADAM8 and ADAM9. Recombinant HB-EGF increased fibroblast αSMA and proliferation, reduced cardiosphere beating frequency without changing size, reduced contractility of human heart slices, and increased PDGFRα+ area and collagen deposition — phenocopying the silenced-monocyte supernatant. Supernatant from silenced monocytes induced EGFR and Akt phosphorylation in fibroblasts; gefitinib prevented the αSMA induction without affecting basal αSMA or causing cytotoxicity and reversed the cardiosphere contraction deficit, and HB-EGF neutralizing antibodies reduced the paracrine activation [Evidence: Functional perturbation (recombinant ligand, receptor inhibition, ligand neutralization)]
CF041-INT-F04 (Hematopoietic DNMT3A-R882H cells → remote myocardium): Infarct sizes were comparable by troponin, yet recipients of DNMT3A-R882H marrow had increased interstitial fibrosis in the remote zone with no change in scar size, increased CD68+ cells in the remote zone after infarction (not at baseline), and a non-significant 1.42-fold fibrosis increase at baseline. Their cardiac fibroblasts upregulated Col3a1, Postn, Pdgfra and other profibrotic genes, macrophage subclusters showed increased Ccr2 expression and cell numbers, and the Hbegf+ fraction of the macrophage cluster was increased while Areg was unchanged. In patients, DNMT3A CHIP carriers had significantly increased native T1 without differences in T2, indicating diffuse fibrosis without edema [Evidence: Functional perturbation (mouse bone-marrow transplant) plus observational human imaging]
g.text: Resident-MΦ CCL24 and CHIP-monocyte HB-EGF drive fibroblast

g.title:
miR-21, TGF-β1 and SPP1+ MΦ drive myofibroblasts
CF007-INT-F01 (Myeloid cells ↔ fibroblasts (mutual spatial dependency)): Myeloid and fibroblast abundances showed strong mutual predictive dependency within spots and were co-enriched in a fibrotic niche (niche 4, fibroblast-dominant) and an adjacent inflammatory niche (niche 5, myeloid-dominant); lymphoid–myeloid dependency in the immediate neighbourhood was increased in ischaemic versus myogenic samples [Evidence: Computational prediction from spatial deconvolution]
CF007-INT-F03 (SPP1+ (CD36+) macrophages → fibroblast states, with highest importance for myofibroblasts (Fib2, POSTN+)): SPP1+ macrophage marker expression predicted all fibroblast states better than other myeloid states, with the highest importance for myofibroblasts both within a spot and in the local neighbourhood; myofibroblast marker expression aligned with a gradient of SPP1+ macrophage markers, and in situ hybridization in an independent cohort confirmed CD163+SPP1+ macrophages adjacent to myofibroblasts, with SPP1+ macrophages enriched in disease [Evidence: Computational prediction with independent in situ spatial validation]
CF007-INT-F04 (SPP1+ macrophages → myofibroblasts (Fib2); SPP1+ macrophages → Fib3): Crosstalk between SPP1+ macrophages and Fib2 was predicted to change with disease stage, with increased PDGF-C, PDGF-D and THBS1 signalling in ischaemic versus myogenic samples and increased ADAM17 and TGFB1 in fibrotic versus myogenic samples; enhanced TGFβ1 signalling toward Fib3 was predicted in ischaemic versus myogenic samples [Evidence: Computational prediction]
CF011-INT-F03 (LYVE1+, monocyte-derived and antigen-presenting macrophages → FB4 fibroblasts): Macrophage populations were predicted to interact with FB4 via CD74–MIF; four spots were identified in the public Visium dataset co-expressing FN1, LYVE1, CD74 and MIF, as predicted [Evidence: Computational prediction with limited spatial co-expression support]
CF011-INT-F05 (C1QA+ macrophages ↔ PTX3+ FB3 fibroblasts (proximity only)): C1QA+ macrophages were imaged adjacent to PTX3+ FB3 fibroblasts, which the authors describe as suggesting cross-talk between the two cell types [Evidence: Observational (colocalization)]
CF050-INT-F01 (Not a sender–receiver pair (cell-type-specific miRNA abundance)): miR-21 was the single highest-expressed microRNA in cardiac macrophages, constituting about a quarter of all microRNA molecules in that cell type and far exceeding levels in fibroblasts and other fractions; it increased progressively at 6 and 21 days after TAC and had the highest microRNA-to-targetome ratio among macrophage microRNAs in both sham and disease. Cx3cr1-Cre × miR-21flox mice had over 90% reduction of macrophage miR-21 with preserved levels in other cardiac, myeloid and lymphoid cells and normal baseline cardiac function [Evidence: Observational (quantitative small RNA sequencing) plus genetic model validation]
CF050-INT-F02 (Macrophage miR-21 → myocardial fibrosis and function): Macrophage-specific miR-21 deletion significantly prevented TAC-induced fibrosis and cardiac hypertrophy at organ and cellular level, reduced hypertrophy- and fibrosis-related gene expression, and preserved ejection fraction, anterior wall thickness and radial strain (approaching sham levels). Macrophage numbers were reduced in TAC-treated knockout hearts while peripheral blood mononuclear cell counts were unchanged [Evidence: Functional perturbation (macrophage-specific conditional deletion)]
CF050-INT-F03 (miR-21 → macrophage polarisation state): Macrophage-specific miR-21 deletion increased the relative fraction of M2-like macrophages with upregulated cell cycle genes, confirmed by reduced total macrophage number, increased M2-like fraction and increased BrdU incorporation in M2-like cells at day 3 after TAC; inflammation-associated genes upregulated after pressure overload in wild-type macrophages were largely repressed in knockouts across both M1-like and M2-like subclusters. In cultured BMDM, LNA-anti-miR-21 significantly reduced LPS-induced Il6, Nos2 and Tnf [Evidence: Functional perturbation (genetic in vivo, antisense in vitro)]
CF050-INT-F04 (M1-like macrophages → Postn+ activated fibroblasts): Under pressure overload the dominant changes in predicted interaction were between M1-like macrophages and Postn+ activated fibroblasts, and these macrophage-to-fibroblast signals were the most significantly repressed in miR-21 knockout TAC hearts (5 of 8 candidate ligands passed the regulation threshold), with reduced ligand gene expression confirmed by qPCR in LV myocardium. One pathway, Lrp1-dependent signalling, was instead activated in the knockouts [Evidence: Computational prediction with transcript-level confirmation]
CF050-INT-F05 (Proinflammatory macrophages → cardiac fibroblasts (myofibroblast transformation)): Macrophage miR-21 deletion specifically repressed myofibroblast transformation, with fewer myofibroblasts and loss of the RNA-velocity-inferred progression from Postn+ activated fibroblasts toward Acta2+/Tcf21 myofibroblasts. In co-culture, unstimulated quiescent macrophages did not induce myofibroblast transformation and miR-21 inhibition had no effect under those conditions, whereas LPS-polarised macrophages drove strong myofibroblast transformation that was significantly reduced by LNA-anti-miR-21 pretreatment [Evidence: Functional perturbation (defined co-culture plus genetic/antisense manipulation of the sender)]
CF051-INT-F03 (Cardiac macrophages → cardiac fibroblasts): Macrophages from TAC hearts increased IL-6 and IL-10 production and Tgfb1 expression and released higher amounts of most measured cytokines and growth factors including TGF-β1 and IL-10. Both TGF-β1 and IL-10 showed dose-dependent stimulation of myofibroblast differentiation, myofibroblast growth and collagen production at concentrations produced by cardiac macrophages ex vivo [Evidence: Functional perturbation (exogenous recombinant cytokine addition) plus observational secretion data]
g.text: miR-21, TGF-β1 and SPP1+ MΦ drive myofibroblasts
MΦ miR-21 deletion prevents TAC fibrosis; SPP1+ MΦ sit beside

g.data-finding-ids: CF042-INT-F01 CF042-INT-F02 CF042-INT-F03 CF042-INT-F04 CF042-INT-F05 CF044-INT-F01 CF044-INT-F02 CF044-INT-F03 CF044-INT-F04 CF051-INT-F02 CF051-INT-F05 CF052-INT-F01 CF052-INT-F06 CF054-INT-F01 CF054-INT-F02 CF054-INT-F03 CF054-INT-F04
g.title:
Anti-fibrotic: CST3, GATA6+, resident MΦ
CF042-INT-F01 (Human pericardial fluid immune cells → human cardiac fibroblasts): Co-culture with patient-derived pericardial fluid cells reduced baseline fibroblast gel contraction and blunted TGF-β1-induced activation; adding cells back to their own acellular pericardial fluid blunted that fluid's fibroblast-activating capacity. Pericardial cells from patients without flow-limiting CAD had significantly greater antifibrotic capacity than cells from patients with recent MI [Evidence: Functional perturbation (human co-culture)]
CF042-INT-F02 (Pericardial macrophage subsets (identity and injury response)): Five macrophage clusters were identified; cluster 0 (FN1+) was proportionally reduced after MI and clusters 0 and 1 carried almost all the differential expression between groups, while clusters 10, 14 and 16 changed little. Velocity analysis showed two trajectories defined by FN1 and CCL2, with NOCAD vectors longer and directed toward the FN1hi state and the CCL2hi-to-FN1hi lineage connection lost after MI; GATA6 was enriched in FN1hi macrophages but expressed by only about 5% of them. Flow cytometry confirmed CD163hiFN1+ macrophages (TIM4+, LYVE1+) were enriched in NOCAD patients. SCENIC predicted IRF2 and HOXB6 as drivers of cluster 0 and PPARG, MXD1 and XBP1 of cluster 1, and NICHES predicted FN1-, PDGFB-, C3- and WNT5A-related signalling enriched in cluster 0/NOCAD and CCL2- and CALM-related signalling in cluster 1/MI, with PLAU and VEGFA equally represented [Evidence: Observational (human single-cell) with computational regulatory and signalling inference]
CF042-INT-F03 (FN1+ pericardial macrophages → human cardiac fibroblasts): Enriched FN1+ pericardial macrophages reproduced the antifibrotic effect of total pericardial cells whereas enriched pericardial T cells did not, and the inhibitory action was preserved and even enhanced across a Transwell, supporting a paracrine mechanism. CST3 was the second highest differentially expressed secreted factor enriched in NOCAD cluster 0 macrophages, was higher in FN1+ than FN1− pericardial macrophages at protein level, was released more by total pericardial cells and FN1+ macrophages than by T cells, and was secreted significantly less by MI than NOCAD macrophages. CST3 antibody blockade abrogated the antifibrotic capacity of pericardial cells [Evidence: Functional perturbation (cell enrichment, Transwell separation, antibody blockade) in human cells]
CF042-INT-F04 (Myeloid-derived CST3 → infarct and border-zone fibrosis): Cst3 was reduced in pericardial and cardiac macrophages (Ly6Chi monocytes had low basal Cst3, unchanged) with reduced circulating and pericardial CST3; baseline cardiac function, infarct size and myeloid recruitment were unaffected. At day 7, α-SMA and collagen I showed a numerical increase in infarct and border zones that did not reach significance. At day 28, total scar size was unchanged but border-zone fibrosis was increased, with worse function (higher EDPVR, lower ESPVR and preload recruitable stroke work) [Evidence: Functional perturbation (conditional gene deletion) with an explicit non-significant intermediate result]
CF042-INT-F05 (FN1+ macrophages in the heart (relationship to pericardial FN1+ macrophages)): FN1+ macrophages in the human heart were enriched within the SPP1+ macrophage cluster and found primarily in ischemic regions rather than healthy myogenic or fibrotic tissue; consistent with the pericardial findings, cardiac FN1+ macrophages expressed lower CST3 than resident cardiac macrophage and monocyte populations [Evidence: Observational (reused external dataset; flagged)]
CF044-INT-F01 (GATA6+ pericardial macrophages → pericardial granulocyte recruitment): LysCreGATA6fl/fl mice developed significantly more severe pericarditis with more nuclei in the perimyocardial region and greater average pericardial thickness (maximum thickness unchanged). In whole heart they had lower proportions of B cells, neutrophils and CD64+F4/80+ cells and higher Ly6G+SiglecF+ granulocytes and eosinophils, with fewer Ly6C+CCR2− monocytes and more Ly6C−CCR2+ macrophages within the myeloid gate. In separated tissue, neutrophils, Ly6G+SiglecF+ granulocytes and eosinophils were increased and B cells decreased in the pericardium, with no significant differences in the myocardium [Evidence: Functional perturbation (conditional gene deletion)]
CF044-INT-F02 (GATA6+ pericardial macrophages → myocardial inflammation (tested, largely not supported)): At day 3 after MI, absence of GATA6+ pericardial macrophages increased the proportion of Ly6C−CCR2+ macrophages and decreased Ly6C+CCR2− monocytes, with overall immune cell frequencies in the heart minimally affected. In the pericardial tissue, sham knockouts had more CD3+ T cells and eosinophils and fewer F4/80+ macrophages, and infarcted knockouts had fewer B cells and more γδ T cells and Ly6G+SiglecF+ granulocytes, without altering the severity of inflammation. In CVB3 myocarditis there were no differences in myocarditis score or immune profile and no pericarditis in either group [Evidence: Functional perturbation with largely negative results]
CF044-INT-F03 (GATA6+ pericardial macrophages → post-MI fibrosis and remodelling): Overall fibrosis across the whole heart cross-section was significantly higher in LysCreGATA6fl/fl mice, but there were no significant differences in fibrotic area in the infarct zone, the border zone or the remote zone, where both genotypes showed very limited fibrosis apart from one mouse per group. No significant change was seen in average or minimum LV thickness, ejection fraction, LVIDD, fractional shortening, septal or posterior wall thickness, or ECG waveforms [Evidence: Functional perturbation with a partially negative result]
CF044-INT-F04 (GATA6+ vs bone-marrow-derived macrophages → fibroblasts): Bone-marrow-derived macrophages, but not GATA6+ macrophages, upregulated CCL2, CCL11, CXCL9, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-10 and MMP12 in response to LPS, and induced fibroblasts to upregulate CCL2, CCL11, MMP9 and MMP12. GATA6+ macrophages instead caused a non-significant trend to increased fibroblast GM-CSF and a significant downregulation of fibroblast α-SMA, and had lower TIMP2 regardless of stimulation. GATA6+ pericardial macrophages expressed the RGD-binding integrin αVβ3 while myocardial macrophages expressed the laminin receptor α6β1, with β2, β3 and β5 present only on pericardial macrophages [Evidence: Functional perturbation (co-culture with defined stimulation) plus observational phenotyping]
CF051-INT-F02 (Resident macrophages → cardiac fibroblasts/ECM (restraint of fibrosis)): α-CD115 preferentially depleted resident macrophages (sustained through the first week) while monocyte-derived macrophages recovered from circulating monocytes, with near-complete loss of CD163+ cells and no effect on other immune cell types. Depletion did not alter hypertrophy, ejection fraction or fractional shortening at 1 week, but fibrosis after TAC was further aggravated; by 6 weeks, despite complete restoration of cardiac immune cells, depleted mice showed aggravated fibrosis and depressed cardiac function [Evidence: Functional perturbation (antibody-mediated depletion)]
CF051-INT-F05 (Monocyte-derived macrophages → fibrosis (profibrotic); resident macrophages → counteracting): Resident macrophage depletion alone aggravated fibrosis in wild-type mice; isotype-treated CCR2 knockout mice showed the lowest fibrosis, consistent with a profibrotic role of recruited macrophages; α-CD115-treated CCR2 knockout mice lacking both populations were protected from the increased fibrosis. Unexpectedly, CCR2 knockout mice did not show a blunted angiogenic response when resident macrophages were depleted [Evidence: Functional perturbation (combined depletion and genetic deletion) with an unexplained dissociation]
CF052-INT-F01 (CCR2− resident macrophages → myocardial tissue/cardiomyocytes (organ-level requirement)): Depletion selectively removed CCR2− macrophages without affecting neutrophils, monocytes or CCR2+ macrophages and reduced survival in Tnnt2DK210/DK210 mice; it attenuated LV dilation, increased relative wall thickness, reduced stroke volume, reduced circumferential LV enlargement and compact myocardial expansion, and reduced cardiomyocyte lengthening (width increase preserved), without altering ejection fraction or myocardial contractility. Cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area, interstitial fibrosis (minimal at these stages) and Nppa/Nppb/Myh7 expression were similar between depleted and non-depleted mutants [Evidence: Functional perturbation (depletion)]
CF052-INT-F06 (CCR2− resident macrophages → myocardium (fibrosis and remodelling)): TAC in CD169-DTR mice produced greater reduction in LV systolic function, attenuated LV dilation despite equal LV mass increase (concentric rather than eccentric hypertrophy), exaggerated myocardial fibrosis, elevated Anp, Bnp and Myh6 expression, and diminished coronary microvascular growth; no differences were seen between sham-treated control and CD169-DTR mice [Evidence: Functional perturbation (depletion, second model)]
CF054-INT-F01 (Pericardial compartment (tissue/cells collectively) → myocardium): Infarct sizes were similar between approaches and ejection fraction fell in both; mice with an intact pericardium had lower EDPVR (less LV stiffness), improved relaxation (Tau, dP/dtmin) and better PRSW and dP/dtmax, while ESPVR was not improved. Sham pericardial disruption without ligation did not alter these parameters [Evidence: Functional perturbation (surgical)]
CF054-INT-F02 (Gata6+ pericardial cavity macrophages (GPCMs) — population identity): GPCMs (MHCII−CD102+) were the most abundant pericardial immune cell at steady state and were also present, more abundantly, in pig and human pericardial fluid; myeloid Gata6 deletion specifically depleted them without affecting pericardial MHCII+ myeloid cells or dendritic cells. GPCMs were transcriptionally similar to pleural and peritoneal cavity macrophages (no differentially expressed genes versus pleural, 33 versus peritoneal) but differed from cardiac macrophages in thousands of genes, with cardiac macrophages enriched for extracellular matrix organization and inflammatory mediator genes and pericardial macrophages for metabolic processes [Evidence: Observational (transcriptomic and cytometric)]
CF054-INT-F03 (Pericardial cavity GPCMs → infarcted myocardium (epicardial surface and infarct zone)): GPCMs disappeared from pericardial lavage at days 3–7 with rebound by day 28, coincident with neutrophil and Ly6Chi monocyte influx into the pericardium; Venus+ GPCMs were recruited to the mesothelial layer by day 7 and were found only in the infarcted region, penetrating past the epicardial surface, and bead-labelled pericardial cells appeared in the heart after MI. GATA6 and CD102 protein were reduced on entering the tissue, and CCR2 deletion did not affect CD102+ macrophage recruitment to the heart [Evidence: Observational with cell labelling (bone marrow chimerism and bead transfer); not formal fate mapping]
CF054-INT-F04 (GPCMs → remote myocardium collagen deposition (fibroblast activity inferred, not measured directly)): Infarct sizes and ejection fraction decline were similar between genotypes and neutrophil, Ly6Chi monocyte and Ly6Clo macrophage numbers in the heart were equal at baseline and after MI. Lyz2Cre;Gata6fl/fl mice showed elevated EDPVR (stiffer LV) and a trend toward reduced PRSW. Total LV fibrotic area by Sirius red did not differ between groups, but regional analysis showed enhanced interstitial fibrosis in the remote myocardium by Sirius red and collagen I staining [Evidence: Functional perturbation (conditional gene deletion)]
g.text: Pericardial MΦ CST3 blunts TGF-β; losing resident MΦ ↑ fibrosis

g.title:
VEGF-A, IGF1, VEGF-C build vessels
CF051-INT-F04 (Cardiac macrophages → endothelial cells (angiogenesis)): Macrophages from TAC hearts increased Vegfa expression; microvascular density rose after TAC and this increase was blunted by α-CD115 depletion. Isolated cardiac macrophages stimulated HUVEC tube formation (mesh area, nodes, junctions, meshes), and recombinant VEGF-A produced a dose-dependent stimulation of tube formation [Evidence: Functional perturbation (depletion in vivo; co-culture and recombinant ligand in vitro)]
CF052-INT-F02 (CCR2− resident macrophages → coronary endothelium/vasculature): Tnnt2DK210/DK210 hearts showed marked coronary arterial expansion and increased microvascular density relative to controls; both were markedly reduced after CCR2− macrophage depletion [Evidence: Functional perturbation (depletion)]
CF052-INT-F03 (CCR2− resident macrophages → candidate endothelial and cardiomyocyte receivers (not demonstrated)): CCR2− macrophages expressed growth factors and mechanosensing-associated genes (Igf1, Hbegf, Bmp2, Cyr61, Pdgfc, Fgf9, Trpv4) whereas CCR2+ macrophages expressed inflammatory mediators, integrins, Vegfa, Pgf and matrix genes; Igf1, Pdgfc, Cyr61 and Hbegf increased in CCR2− macrophages from failing hearts, and macrophage IGF1 and CYR61 protein increased in Tnnt2DK210/DK210 hearts, which was absent after depletion [Evidence: Observational (expression) within a perturbation framework]
CF078-INT-F01 (Apoptotic cells → macrophages): Vegfc rose over time after apoptotic cell uptake, comparably to LPS stimulation, with increased VEGFC protein and secreted VEGFC. Cd36 deficiency reduced both efferocytosis and the Vegfc increase; blocking engulfment with cytochalasin D abolished induction, while inhibiting fatty acid oxidation with etomoxir did not. ChIP-Seq showed an activated Vegfc locus during efferocytosis with a STAT6 footprint, STAT6 inhibition impaired induction, and Cd36-deficient macrophages had less phosphorylated STAT6 [Evidence: Functional perturbation (genetic deletion and pharmacological inhibition in vitro)]
g.text: Resident MΦ sustain microvascular growth; efferocytosis induces

g.data-finding-ids: CF006-INT-F03 CF029-INT-F04 CF045-INT-F01 CF045-INT-F02 CF045-INT-F03 CF045-INT-F04 CF045-INT-F05 CF045-INT-F06 CF045-INT-F07 CF045-INT-F08 CF051-INT-F01 CF087-INT-F02 CF087-INT-F06
g.title:
Secrete matrix, but do not become FBs
CF006-INT-F03 (Monocyte-derived inflammatory macrophage/monocyte states → candidate fibroblast receiver (not demonstrated)): Tissue-resident macrophage signature (MRC1, CD163, LYVE1, F13A1, VSIG4) was reduced and CD163+ cells decreased by in situ hybridization in DCM, while intermediate monocytes and TREM2, CCL3 and KLF2 macrophage states expressing IL1A, IL1B, TNF, AREG and EREG expanded; trajectory analysis predicted these states to be monocyte-derived [Evidence: Observational plus computational trajectory prediction]
CF029-INT-F04 (Monocyte/macrophage populations (identity and flux)): Twelve populations showed significant flux between conditions: F-SL and F-SH fibroblasts dropped sharply at MI-day 3 while M1 and M2 macrophage populations expanded at days 3 and 7, and myofibroblasts appeared at day 7. Tissue-resident macrophages were resolved into a TIMD4+LYVE1+MHC-IIlow subset persisting after injury and an MHC-IIhigh subset, and an interferon-inducible macrophage population (MAC-IFNIC) was identified; all minor sham monocyte/macrophage populations aligned with monocyte-derived populations that influx after MI [Evidence: Observational with a purpose-built statistical test]
CF045-INT-F01 (CX3CR1+ macrophages → PDGFRα+ fibroblasts (conversion tested, not supported)): MI caused a marked (approximately threefold at 7 days, further increased at 28 days) expansion of PDGFRα+ fibroblasts and a peak in CX3CR1-derived cell density at 7 days, yet macrophage-derived fibroblasts accounted for less than 1% of fibroblasts in control and infarcted hearts at all timepoints; the same was true in normal atria and ventricles and in kidney, lung and liver [Evidence: Lineage tracing (important negative result)]
CF045-INT-F02 (CX3CR1+ macrophages → endothelial cells, myofibroblasts, mural cells (conversion tested, not supported); macrophage identity retention): CX3CR1-derived cells showed no overlap with CD31+ endothelial cells and did not contribute to α-SMA+ myofibroblast or vascular mural cell populations; approximately 93% of CX3CR1-derived infarct cells were LyzM+ at 7 days and about 76% at 28 days, with similar results for Mac2 [Evidence: Lineage tracing (negative result)]
CF045-INT-F03 (Myeloid cells (identity genes) — no sender–receiver pair): Myeloid clusters expressed Vim but negligible Tcf21, Fap, Pdgfra, Pdgfrb and Acta2, with no consistent upregulation after infarction; Vim was significantly reduced in most myeloid clusters after MI; reparative macrophages showed a statistically significant but very low increase in Tcf21; S100a4 (FSP-1) was expressed predominantly by macrophages. Conversely, fibroblasts increased Lyz2 at 3–7 days after MI but did not express detectable Itgam, Adgre1, Csf1r, Cx3cr1, Ptprc or Cd68 [Evidence: Observational (own and reused single-cell datasets; flagged reused dataset)]
CF045-INT-F04 (Macrophages → fibroblasts (candidate; ligand source only)): Macrophages expressed significantly higher Tgfb1, Pdgfb, Mmp8, Mmp9, Mmp12 and Mmp13 than fibroblasts, whereas fibroblasts expressed significantly higher Mmp2, Mmp3, Mmp11, Mmp14, Mmp23, Timp1, Timp2, Timp3, Tgfb2, Tgfb3 and Bmp4 [Evidence: Observational (reused dataset)]
CF045-INT-F05 (Macrophage and monocyte subsets → extracellular matrix): Infarct macrophages expressed low levels of structural collagens (Col1a1, Col3a1, Col5a1 significantly reduced at 3 days versus sham, no difference at 7 days) but markedly induced Spp1 and Thbs1 at 3 and 7 days and expressed Emilin2, Vcan, Ecm1 and Fn1; reparative macrophages expressed higher Sparc, Spp1 and Col14a1, inflammatory macrophages and Mp5 were the main source of Thbs1, and monocytes plus inflammatory macrophages were the main source of Emilin2, Vcan and Fn1; Postn was essentially restricted to activated fibroblasts with only a modest myeloid increase at 7 days. Fn1-high and Spp1-high macrophages co-expressed other matricellular genes [Evidence: Observational (own plus reused dataset)]
CF045-INT-F06 (Macrophages → extracellular matrix (protein level)): Sham hearts had negligible OPN and TSP-1 immunoreactivity; after infarction abundant macrophages expressed OPN (peaking at 3 days) and TSP-1 (increased at 3–7 days), with macrophages the predominant but not exclusive OPN source; fibronectin-expressing macrophages were also present at 7 days, though fibronectin was localised in other cell types and deposited in the matrix network [Evidence: Observational (protein localisation)]
CF045-INT-F07 (Myeloid cells → extracellular matrix; fibroblasts → extracellular matrix): Fibroblasts expressed much higher fibrillar and basement membrane collagens, FN1, VCAN and SPARC than myeloid cells across all zones; POSTN was significantly higher in fibroblasts only in infarct, border and fibrotic zones; myeloid cells were the predominant source of EMILIN2 and SPP1 in human infarcted myocardium and expressed higher THBS1 than fibroblasts [Evidence: Observational (reused external dataset; flagged)]
CF045-INT-F08 (Myeloid cells (bulk) → extracellular matrix): 7-day infarct myeloid cells showed increased Col1a1, Col1a2, Col3a1, Col5a1 and Col5a2, increased Fn1 (peaking at 3 days) and increased Postn, Tnc, Spp1 and Thbs1, while fibroblast-specific Fap, Pdgfra and Tcf21 remained very low and were downregulated after MI; fibrosis-related canonical pathways were among the most enriched [Evidence: Observational (bulk transcriptomics) plus computational upstream regulator prediction]
CF051-INT-F01 (Resident vs monocyte-derived macrophages (identity and effector gene expression)): Cardiac immune cells, predominantly macrophages, expanded at 1 week after TAC and returned to sham levels by 4 weeks; 8 of 12 macrophage clusters changed abundance. Resident macrophages were distinguished by Lyve1, Cd163, Timd4 and multiple C-C chemokines including Ccl24, whereas monocyte-derived macrophages expressed MHC-II genes and the fibrosis-mediating genes Spp1, Thbs1 and Fn1. IL10RA, IL4, STAT3 and IRF2 were predicted as activated upstream regulators in resident macrophages, with IFNG, IRF3 and IRF7 predicted inhibited [Evidence: Observational (cytometry and transcriptomics) with computational upstream-regulator prediction]
CF087-INT-F02 (TRMPs → all cardiac cell types in the assembloid): TRMPs were predicted to interact with all cardiac cell types, with SPP1 featuring in seven of the top 20 predicted interactions; SPP1 protein colocalized with CD45+CD163+ TRMPs. The top 18 TRMP ligands were more highly expressed in assembloids than organoids, with GO terms for epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, complement, angiogenesis, inflammation and myogenesis [Evidence: Computational prediction with expression-level validation]
CF087-INT-F06 (TRMPs → extracellular matrix / fibroblast compartment): Collagen fibril organization genes were upregulated in assembloids; COL1A1 showed broader spatial distribution with reduced entropy (more uniform expression) and increased COL1A1 transcript levels in assembloids relative to organoids [Evidence: Observational]

g.data-finding-ids: CF004-INT-F05 CF006-INT-F04 CF007-INT-F08 CF007-INT-F09 CF026-INT-F01 CF037-INT-F01 CF037-INT-F02 CF037-INT-F03 CF037-INT-F04 CF037-INT-F05 CF060-INT-F01 CF060-INT-F02
g.title:
Activated POSTN+ / THBS4+ states
CF004-INT-F05 (Fibroblasts (disease-associated) → ECM compartment): Fibroblasts showed the largest number of differentially expressed genes of any cell type and increased expression of ECM organization and collagen formation genes; fibroblast proportion from snRNA-seq corresponded with trichrome-quantified fibrosis, while the compositional increase in fibroblasts itself was non-significant [Evidence: Observational]
CF006-INT-F04 (Fibroblasts (DCM activated state) → ECM compartment): DCM fibroblasts displayed an activation signature (FAP, CTGF, LUM, ACTB, COL1A1, BGN, MGP) and upregulated POSTN, MEOX1/2, TLL1, EDNRA, SVEP1 and FRZB, with enrichment of ECM synthesis and organization pathways; donor fibroblasts selectively expressed GPX3, PID1, TGFBR3, ACSM3, APOD [Evidence: Observational]
CF007-INT-F08 (PDGFRβ-lineage mesenchymal cells → myofibroblasts (Fib2)): The Fib2 population and collagen/ECM genes increased over time after MI while Fib1 decreased, supporting a differentiation trajectory from SCARA5+ fibroblasts (Fib1) to myofibroblasts (Fib2); a corresponding pseudotime trajectory with increasing ECM score was inferred in the human samples [Evidence: Lineage tracing (mouse) plus computational trajectory inference (human)]
CF007-INT-F09 (Cell-intrinsic (no sender cell)): RUNX1 overexpression increased myofibroblast differentiation and matrix expression [Evidence: Functional perturbation (gain of function, cell culture)]
CF026-INT-F01 (Not a sender–receiver pair (emergent fibroblast states)): Two fibroblast populations essentially absent from unstressed hearts (Fibroblast-Cilp and Fibroblast-Thbs4) expanded markedly with angiotensin II, expressed high periostin and the greatest summed ECM-remodelling transcript abundance, and did not correspond to ACTA2+ myofibroblasts. Flow cytometry detected no significant fibroblast increase and cell-cycle scoring showed no significant proliferation increase, suggesting a state change in resident fibroblasts; RNA velocity indicated Fibroblast-Thbs4 arises predominantly from Fibroblast-Cilp. THBS4+ cells were aggregated in interstitial foci and absent around perivascular lesions [Evidence: Observational with computational trajectory inference]
CF037-INT-F01 (Macrophages ↔ myofibroblasts (circuit-level relationship)): After MI, macrophages and myofibroblasts both rose and peaked around day 7, after which macrophage counts and activation declined to baseline (TIM4+ resident macrophages depleted then restored by day 65) while myofibroblasts remained elevated through day 28 — the pattern defined as cold fibrosis, with a myofibroblast-to-macrophage ratio of about 6:1. Around the surgical suture, macrophages and myofibroblasts were both abundant (ratio near 1:1), consistent with a foreign-body response and hot fibrosis [Evidence: Observational (lineage tracing and quantitative spatial histology) within a modelling framework]
CF037-INT-F02 (Macrophages ↔ myofibroblasts in interstitial and replacement fibrosis): TAC produced extensive fibrosis with reduced cardiomyocyte numbers in all fibrosis types; myofibroblasts were elevated in all fibrotic regions and highest in replacement fibrosis, and macrophages were elevated to a similar extent in both interstitial and replacement fibrosis (perivascular regions showed only a trend for macrophages), giving a myofibroblast-to-macrophage ratio near 1:1 consistent with hot fibrosis [Evidence: Observational (lineage tracing and quantitative histology)]
CF037-INT-F03 (Myeloid cells and fibroblasts/myofibroblasts (relative abundance over time)): In human hearts, myeloid cell abundance increased within the first two weeks after MI and returned to baseline by 30+ days, while fibroblasts and myofibroblasts increased and remained high — a cold fibrosis pattern. In saline-treated pigs, macrophage abundance rose at day 3 and declined by day 28 while myofibroblast abundance stayed high, whereas rhAgrin-treated pig hearts showed both populations returning to baseline by day 28 with less fibrosis, matching the modelled healing trajectory [Evidence: Computational deconvolution of observational human and pig transcriptomics (human dataset reused, flagged)]
CF037-INT-F04 (Myofibroblasts → myofibroblasts (autocrine); macrophages → fibroblasts/myofibroblasts (paracrine, declining)): The strongest inferred growth-factor interaction was the myofibroblast autocrine loop, which increased from day 3 to day 28 while all macrophage-involving interactions decreased. ParTI showed fibroblasts at day 28 almost exclusively occupying a fibrosis/ECM-deposition task while macrophage states returned toward homeostatic distribution. In human MI, TIMP1–POSTN spatial co-expression increased and stayed high at 30+ days; Timp1 was expressed almost exclusively by myofibroblasts, peaking at day 3 in parallel with myofibroblast proliferation and persisting to day 28 in mice and pigs [Evidence: Computational prediction (on reused datasets) with spatial co-expression support]
CF037-INT-F05 (Myofibroblast-derived TIMP1 → myofibroblasts (autocrine)): Recombinant mouse TIMP1 increased myofibroblast EdU incorporation and anti-TIMP1 reduced it; recombinant human full-length and N-terminal TIMP1 both increased primate fibroblast proliferation. In vivo, anti-TIMP1 reduced proliferating lineage-traced myofibroblasts without affecting macrophage abundance, macrophage proliferation or the Galectin-3+ pro-fibrotic macrophage fraction, and did not significantly reduce the αSMA+ myofibroblast fraction (slight trend only). At 35 days, anti-TIMP1 reduced the number of sections with detectable scar and transmural scars, with no significant difference in ejection fraction or fractional shortening [Evidence: Functional perturbation (recombinant ligand and neutralizing antibody, in vitro and in vivo)]
CF060-INT-F01 (Fibroblast subsets → ECM (ECM-Fib as the dominant matrix source)): Fibroblasts had the highest ECM score of all niche cells; an ECM-Fib subtype increased continuously after TAC and carried the highest ECM score, with Fib1 and ECM-Fib the top collagen expressers. Thbs4 was highly specific to injury-activated ECM-Fib, with THBS4 protein marking a subpopulation of fate-traced cells only in injured hearts and showing focal expansion matching patchy interstitial fibrosis; THBS4 in PDGFRα+ fibroblasts was confirmed in human heart failure tissue. No fibroblast proliferation was detected, and RNA velocity and trajectory analysis suggested Fib1 as the origin of ECM-Fib [Evidence: Observational with computational trajectory inference and protein/in situ validation]
CF060-INT-F02 (Cell-intrinsic transcription factor (no sender cell)): TEAD1 activity was predicted to be highest in ECM-Fib and among the transcription factors most correlated with the ECM score, together with MEIS1, RUNX2 and NCOA3; TGF-β, hypoxia and VEGF pathway activity increased across fibroblast subtypes after TAC, strongest in ECM-Fib. Retroviral Tead1 overexpression strongly induced Acta2, Col1a1 and Fn1 independent of TGF-β stimulation [Evidence: Computational prediction plus functional perturbation (gain of function, cell line)]

g.data-finding-ids: CF017-INT-F03 CF017-INT-F04 CF017-INT-F05 CF021-INT-F02 CF022-INT-F01 CF022-INT-F05
g.title:
Intrinsic brakes set TGF-β sensitivity
CF017-INT-F03 (Exogenous TGF-β1 (sender not identified) → fibroblasts): On plastic, BAG3−/− CFs showed blunted ACTA2, COL1A1 and FN-EDA responses to TGF-β1; on 8 kPa substrate this inverted, with greater TGF-β1 sensitivity of FN-EDA and COL1A1 and increased collagen secretion, while ACTA2 remained decreased at mRNA and protein level. SMAD2 hyperphosphorylation persisted on soft substrate, siTGFBR2 abolished the reporter hypersensitivity and reduced FN-EDA, and BAG3 knockdown in primary human CFs reproduced the findings [Evidence: Functional perturbation (exogenous ligand, siRNA, substrate control)]
CF017-INT-F04 (Cell-intrinsic (no sender cell)): TGFBR2 was identified as a BAG3 interactor and confirmed by co-IP; lysosomal flux of TGFBR2 did not differ between genotypes whereas proteasomal flux was significantly reduced and V5-TGFBR2 decay was slower in BAG3−/− CFs, with lower TGFBR2 ubiquitination despite unchanged global ubiquitin and paradoxically increased global proteasome activity. BAG3WT but not the DCM-causing BAG3E455K rescued ubiquitination, and BAG3E455K showed reduced TGFBR2 binding [Evidence: Functional perturbation (biochemical, cell culture)]
CF017-INT-F05 (Fibroblasts (BAG3-variant DCM) → ECM / candidate TGF-β axis): Cell types and fibroblast states in BAG3 DCM mirrored other DCM hearts; profibrotic genes (TIMP3, TGFB2, PDGFA, PDGFD) were consistently altered in all DCM fibroblasts, and ENG was significantly upregulated only in BAG3 fibroblasts while DDR2 and FBLN2 were paradoxically downregulated; TGFBR2 mRNA was unchanged in BAG3−/− CFs, and BAG3 LVs showed increased fibrosis and collagen deposition. Differentially expressed genes of hiPSC-CFs and human BAG3 fibroblasts showed no significant overlap overall [Evidence: Observational (human tissue; reused comparison cohorts; flagged)]
CF021-INT-F02 (Mechanical stress → cardiac fibroblasts (Htra3 downregulation); fibroblast Htra3 → extracellular TGF-β1): Htra3 was fibroblast-restricted and downregulated by pressure overload in mice, by mechanical stretch in vitro (with concomitant Tgfb1 increase) and in human failing hearts. Htra3 knockout caused cardiac hypertrophy at baseline and, with TAC, severe heart failure and more fibrosis; fibroblast modules shifted from a quiescent/innate-immunity module toward an ECM/TGF-β module, with Htra3 deletion and TAC acting synergistically. Htra3 overexpression reduced TGF-β1 protein and phospho-Smad2/3, Htra3 bound mature TGF-β1, and phospho-Smad2/3 rose in both fibroblasts and cardiomyocytes with deletion plus TAC. TGF-β-neutralizing antibody ameliorated systolic dysfunction and fibrosis in Htra3 knockout mice after TAC [Evidence: Functional perturbation (germline knockout, overexpression, antibody neutralization) plus binding assay]
CF022-INT-F01 (Cell-intrinsic in cardiac fibroblasts (no sender cell)): Yap and Taz became nuclear in roughly half of vimentin+ myofibroblasts isolated from infarcted hearts, with about 75% of isolated cells αSMA+. Fibroblast-specific Yap/Taz deletion reduced αSMA+ and collagen-I+ fibroblasts, hydroxyproline release, myofibroblast and collagen gene expression and fibroblast proliferation without changing apoptosis, and reduced fibrotic area with preserved ejection fraction, fractional shortening and fractional area change after MI; fibroblast-specific Yap5SA activation produced the opposite, increasing fibrosis and profibrotic gene expression after MI but causing no fibrosis or functional change at baseline [Evidence: Functional perturbation (cell-type-specific deletion and activation) with supporting observational data]
CF022-INT-F05 (Exogenous TGF-β1 and Wnt1 (senders not identified) → cardiac fibroblasts): Both TGF-β1 and Wnt1 induced Yap and Taz protein, and this was blocked by the respective pathway inhibitors. In control fibroblasts both ligands induced Acta2, Col1a1, Axin2, Ephb3, Periostin and Lox, which the inhibitors returned to baseline; in Yap/Taz-deficient fibroblasts TGF-β1 induction of these genes was restricted and Wnt1 failed to induce Acta2, Col1a1, Axin2 and Periostin [Evidence: Functional perturbation (ligand plus inhibitor, in genetically defined cells)]
g.text: BAG3 degrades TGFBR2; HTRA3 cleaves TGF-β1; Yap/Taz–TEAD

g.title:
IL-33/ST2 and Yap/Taz secretome recruit MΦ
CF006-INT-F02 (Fibroblast subpopulation Fb7 (CCL2) → candidate myeloid receiver (not demonstrated)): A CCL2-expressing fibroblast subpopulation (Fb7) was identified; CCL2-, POSTN- and PCOLCE2-expressing fibroblasts were increased in DCM and localised within the interstitial space between cardiomyocytes, whereas PLA2G2A+ fibroblasts (perivascular/distal vasculature) were enriched in donors and ELN+ Fb5 surrounded epicardial coronary arteries [Evidence: Observational]
CF022-INT-F02 (Cardiac fibroblasts → IL33 production (sender-side regulation)): IL33 was strongly upregulated in fibrotic areas of infarcted hearts; fibroblast Yap/Taz deletion reduced myocardial IL1a, IL6, IL10, IL12b, IL33, St2, IL37 and TNFA, while Yap activation increased IL1a, IL33, IL6 and TnfA. Human cardiac fibroblasts increased IL33 expression and secretion in response to H2O2 or TGF-β1, and this was abrogated by verteporfin. Yap and Taz activated the IL33 promoter dose-dependently; this required TEAD binding (blocked by dominant-negative TEAD1, verteporfin and TEAD-site mutation), Yap bound the IL33 promoter by ChIP, and co-expression of active MST1 or LATS2 but not their kinase-inactive mutants abolished activation [Evidence: Functional perturbation (promoter and chromatin assays, pharmacological inhibition) in mouse and human cells]
CF022-INT-F03 (Cardiac fibroblasts → macrophages/monocytes): Fibroblast-specific Yap/Taz deletion reduced F4/80+ macrophages in the infarct and border zone at 5 and 28 days and reduced the proportion of Ly6Chi monocytes at 3 days. Conditioned medium from Yap/Taz-deficient fibroblasts inhibited macrophage migration relative to control fibroblast medium and reduced pro-inflammatory M1 gene expression in treated macrophages, while some M2 genes were upregulated [Evidence: Functional perturbation (sender-side genetic deletion plus conditioned-medium transfer)]
CF022-INT-F04 (Exogenous IL33 (physiological sender not identified here) → fibroblasts and macrophages; Yap-driven fibroblast programme → ST2-dependent output): Recombinant IL33 induced stress fibres, αSMA, SM22α and collagen I in cardiac fibroblasts and increased macrophage IL1b, IL6, Ccr7, Rantes and Nos2 as well as the profibrotic genes Acta2, Col1a1 and Fn1. Blocking ST2 abrogated the TGF-β1-induced expression of Acta2, Tagln, Col1a1, IL6 and Ctgf in Yap-activated fibroblasts and reduced αSMA and collagen-I staining [Evidence: Functional perturbation (exogenous cytokine; receptor blockade in vitro)]

g.data-finding-ids: CF011-INT-F04 CF017-INT-F01 CF021-INT-F03 CF021-INT-F04 CF091-INT-F01 CF091-INT-F02 CF091-INT-F03 CF091-INT-F04 CF092-INT-F01 CF092-INT-F02 CF092-INT-F03 CF092-INT-F04
g.title:
TGF-β, stiffness and β-AR act on myocytes
CF011-INT-F04 (FB4 fibroblasts → atrial and ventricular cardiomyocytes): FB4 cells enriched for FN1, COL4A1 and TNC were predicted to interact with different integrins on atrial versus ventricular cardiomyocytes; in skeletal muscle the analogous PRG4+ fibroblast–myocyte interactions instead involved COL1A2, COL6A2 and α10β1 integrins, and skeletal muscle fibroblast–monocyte pairs involved ICAM1–AREG and CXCR4–CXCL12 [Evidence: Computational prediction]
CF017-INT-F01 (Cardiac fibroblasts (BAG3−/−) → cardiomyocytes/tissue function): Fibroblast-restricted BAG3 loss reduced active contractile force and work and increased collagen deposition relative to full wild-type at every fibroblast ratio tested, with greater LDH release; passive tension did not differ between genotypes, and increasing fibroblast content to 40% raised force in wild-type tissues [Evidence: Functional perturbation (genetic, human in vitro)]
CF021-INT-F03 (Fibroblast-derived/ambient TGF-β → cardiomyocytes): Combined Htra3 deletion and TAC drove cardiomyocytes into a state with suppressed mitochondrial and DNA repair genes and activation of TGF-β receptor, small GTPase and p53 modules, with increased γH2A.X and p21; DNA damage also increased in fibroblasts. Nox4 knockdown rescued cardiac dysfunction and reduced DNA damage and TGF-β-related molecules, whereas Nox4 overexpression increased γH2A.X+ cardiomyocytes and worsened dilatation; p53 deletion suppressed TGF-β-related molecules and secretory factors [Evidence: Functional perturbation (AAV-mediated knockdown/overexpression; reused p53 knockout dataset)]
CF021-INT-F04 (Failing cardiomyocytes → circulation (secretory phenotype)): Htra3 was high in the infarct zone and its deletion enlarged the infarct cluster, with ECM genes and cardiomyocyte secretory factors (Bmp1, Tgfb3, Igfbp7) specifically activated there; fibroblast clusters appearing early after MI had low Htra3. AAV9-Htra3 given after TAC inhibited TGF-β signalling and ameliorated dysfunction and fibrosis. Human failing cardiomyocytes showed a conserved module with TGF-β receptor signalling, DNA damage response and the same secretory factors; plasma TGF-β3, LTBP4 and IGFBP7 were higher with heart failure severity and fell after transplantation, and IGFBP7 best separated advanced from non-advanced heart failure while NT-proBNP better diagnosed heart failure [Evidence: Functional perturbation (overexpression) plus observational human transcriptomics and proteomics]
CF091-INT-F01 (Cardiac fibroblasts → cardiomyocytes (tissue integrity)): Cardiomyocytes alone formed loose aggregates, while adding fibroblasts at 1:4 produced compact, spontaneously and synchronously contracting microtissues. Cardiomyocyte genes were detected only in cardiomyocyte-containing microtissues and fibroblast genes in all fibroblast-containing ones, and procollagen I was undetectable in cardiomyocyte-only microtissues, identifying fibroblasts as the collagen source [Evidence: Observational within a defined reconstitution experiment]
CF091-INT-F02 (Exogenous TGF-β1 (sender not identified) → cardiac fibroblasts within a cardiomyocyte-containing tissue): TGF-β1 increased microtissue size and procollagen-I secretion and upregulated most fibrotic genes in fibroblast-containing microtissues, increased vimentin, fibronectin, αSMA, periostin and Ki67, and decreased troponin T and connexin 43, while caspase 3/7 activity was unchanged and IL-6 secretion fell. Cardiomyocyte-specific genes were downregulated in the mixed microtissues but only slightly altered in cardiomyocyte-only microtissues. SD208 blocked TGF-β1-driven growth and collagen production dose-dependently and also reduced procollagen I and profibrotic gene expression in the absence of exogenous TGF-β1 [Evidence: Functional perturbation (exogenous cytokine and receptor inhibitor) in a human tissue model]
CF091-INT-F03 (Activated cardiac fibroblasts → cardiomyocytes (contraction)): TGF-β1 increased contraction rate, reduced contraction amplitude and shortened the relaxation phase. Microtissues assembled from fibroblasts pre-activated before assembly, with no TGF-β1 present afterwards, reproduced the same contraction pattern along with increased size and procollagen-I secretion, indicating that fibroblast activation rather than a direct cytokine effect on cardiomyocytes drives the change. Microtissues containing fibroblasts from heart failure patients likewise contracted faster with a shortened relaxation phase compared with those from unaffected hearts, and responded less often to further TGF-β1 stimulation (one of six vs four of six) [Evidence: Functional perturbation (sender pre-activation before assembly) with a patient-derived cell comparison]
CF091-INT-F04 (Activated cardiac fibroblasts → cardiomyocyte β-adrenoceptor signalling): Fibrotic microtissues remained fully electrically responsive to 3 Hz pacing and showed no change in action potential duration, with only a slightly prolonged depolarization phase and a reduced action potential amplitude interpreted as fewer electrically active cells. Isoproterenol increased contraction rate and shortened contraction and relaxation phases, and nadolol prevented these effects, confirming functional β-adrenoceptors. In the absence of any exogenous agonist, nadolol significantly reduced the contraction rate of fast-beating microtissues containing adult fibroblasts by prolonging relaxation, while its effect on fetal-fibroblast microtissues was slight [Evidence: Functional perturbation (receptor blockade in the absence of exogenous agonist)]
CF092-INT-F01 (Exogenous TGF-β1 (sender not identified) → fibroblast–cardiomyocyte co-culture): TGF-β1-treated tissues showed roughly tenfold higher fibrillar collagen, increased collagen I/III ratio, 2.3-fold higher average stiffness with greater local stiffness heterogeneity, over fourfold higher passive tension, 3.1-fold and 5-fold lower force of contraction at days 14 and 21, higher excitation threshold and significantly higher secreted BNP; no differences were observed in apoptosis, proliferation or the percentage of vimentin- and cTnT-positive cells, indicating the force reduction was not due to cardiomyocyte loss [Evidence: Functional perturbation (exogenous cytokine addition) in human cell culture]
CF092-INT-F02 (Fibroblast–cardiomyocyte co-culture → extracellular matrix): Fibrotic tissues upregulated COL1A2, FN1, THBS1, POSTN, VIM, TGFB1, ACTA2, LOX and CCN2, with enrichment of extracellular matrix, extracellular structure, collagen binding and collagen fibril organization gene sets [Evidence: Observational (within a perturbation model)]
CF092-INT-F03 (Co-culture tissue (mixed cellular source) → extracellular vesicle cargo in medium): Fibrotic tissues showed differential cellular miRNA expression including miR-142 and miR-208, and differential EV miRNA content with increased miR-376a and decreased miR-27a, miR-29b, miR-30a, miR-155 and miR-221; EV size was unchanged. miR-208 was increased in tissue but not in secreted EVs, and miR-221 was unchanged in tissue but significantly decreased in EVs. KEGG analysis of predicted miRNA targets returned ECM–receptor interaction, PI3K-Akt, TGF-β, Hippo, mTOR, gap junction and focal adhesion pathways [Evidence: Observational (profiling) plus computational target prediction]
CF092-INT-F04 (Pharmacological intervention on the fibroblast–cardiomyocyte co-culture): Pirfenidone significantly reduced BNP secretion and average tissue stiffness with reduced stiffness heterogeneity, and downregulated POSTN, LOX, CCN2, THBS1 and collagen type I transcripts, while αSMA and fibronectin were unexpectedly upregulated; collagen content by imaging was unchanged, and force of contraction, passive tension and excitation threshold at day 21 did not differ from untreated fibrotic tissues. A longer two-week treatment significantly decreased passive tension but still had no effect on force of contraction. Standard-of-care drugs decreased BNP secretion without effects on passive or active force at the timepoints treated. Pirfenidone downregulated miR-208 and upregulated miR-221, miR-222, miR-376a and miR-494 in tissue, with miR-221 increased further in EVs [Evidence: Functional perturbation (pharmacological) with important negative results]

g.title:
Myofibroblast exosomes impair angiogenesis
CF029-INT-F01 (Myofibroblasts (MYO), M1 macrophages and MAC-8 → multiple receivers; endothelial cells as dominant receivers): Ninety-one cell–cell relationships exceeded chance; myofibroblasts, M1MF and MAC-8 had the most outbound connections (highest weight for MYO) and endothelial cells by far the most inbound. Fibroblast populations (F-SH, F-SL, F-Act, F-WntX) appeared to communicate exclusively with vascular (endothelial, mural) and glial cells, consistent with imaging showing Pdgfra-GFP+ fibroblasts in close spatial relationship or direct contact with CD31+ endothelial cells. Glial cells communicated with endothelial and mural populations via ligands including Dhh, Sema3b and Sema4f [Evidence: Computational prediction with supporting imaging of proximity]
CF029-INT-F02 (F-WntX fibroblasts → endothelial cell subpopulations): F-WntX was an activated fibroblast state present in sham hearts and persisting after MI, uniquely expressing Wif1 and a strong anti-WNT signature; it was predicted to communicate most significantly with endothelial cells, with top ligands Ptn, Myoc and Timp3 whose corresponding receptors were expressed in endothelial cells but downregulated in F-WntX. WIF1 protein was detected only in the infarct border zone at MI-day 3, not in sham hearts or at days 1 or 7, with about 5% of WIF1+ cells being Pdgfra-GFP+ and about 17% Ki67+; WIF1+ cells were CD31-negative and negative or very low for αSMA [Evidence: Computational prediction with protein-level localisation]
CF062-INT-F01 (Exogenous TGF-β1 (sender not identified) → cardiac fibroblasts): TGF-β1 increased collagen 1α, periostin and fibronectin mRNA, increased phospho-p38 and phospho-SMAD2, and induced αSMA and fibronectin protein, with equivalent responses in adult mouse fibroblasts; TGF-β1 treatment also significantly increased the number of exosomes secreted [Evidence: Functional perturbation (exogenous cytokine, in vitro)]
CF062-INT-F02 (Activated cardiac fibroblasts (myofibroblasts) → cardiac endothelial cells): Exosomes from TGF-β1-activated fibroblasts impaired endothelial tube formation and migration, reduced viability and increased TUNEL+ cells relative to control exosomes; they reduced VEGF-A, CD31 and angiopoietin-1 mRNA and eNOS and Bcl2 protein while increasing HIF1α, and greatly reduced placental growth factor (PIGF) in the angiogenesis array. Control exosomes slightly increased VEGF-A, CD31 and angiopoietin-1 relative to PBS [Evidence: Functional perturbation (exosome transfer, in vitro)]
CF062-INT-F03 (Activated fibroblasts → endothelial cells via exosomal miR-200a-3p): TGF-β1 altered exosomal miRNA content, reducing miR-132-3p and increasing miR-200a-3p and miR-125b-5p, with a similar trend in adult mouse fibroblast exosomes; TGF-β mRNA was not detected in exosomes. Antagomir treatment of the parent fibroblasts reduced exosomal and recipient-endothelial miR-200a-3p and restored PIGF, VEGF-A, angiopoietin-1 and CD31 expression as well as eNOS, ETS-1 and PIGF protein, and attenuated cleaved caspase-3; the PIGF restoration was less than that of VEGF-A [Evidence: Functional perturbation (cargo manipulation in the sender cell)]

g.title:
Injury creates MHC-II+ immunomodulatory ECs
CF057-INT-F01 (Pre-existing cardiac endothelial cells → immunomodulatory endothelial cells (IMECs)): A CD45+CD11b+Cdh5+ hybrid cluster absent at baseline emerged prominently at day 1 after MI and declined by day 28, expressing both endothelial and myeloid genes with high MHC-II but not mesenchymal genes (Cnn1, Serpine1). CD45+ERG+ double-positive cells were found in infarct and border zone after MI and after ischemia/reperfusion; lineage-traced GFP+CD45+ cells peaked at day 3; bone-marrow transplantation yielded very few GFP+ endothelial cells, excluding a circulating bone-marrow origin [Evidence: Observational with lineage tracing and transplantation controls, plus computational trajectory inference]
CF057-INT-F02 (Myeloid cells → IMECs (IL-1β, TNF-α, chemokines); mural cells and fibroblasts → IMECs (TGF-β2); T cells and NK cells → IMECs (IFN-γ)): IMECs showed elevated expression of IL-1β, TNF-α, TGF-β and IFN-γ response gene sets and were predicted to receive IL-1β, chemokine and TGF-β signalling. Tgfb2 came predominantly from mural cells and fibroblasts, Il1b and Tnfa predominantly from myeloid cells, and IFN-γ primarily from T and NK cells; Ifngr1 and Il1r1 were upregulated on endothelial cells from day 1 to day 7 [Evidence: Computational prediction with supporting receptor-expression data]
CF057-INT-F03 (Exogenous TGF-β2 + IL-1β + IFN-γ (senders not identified in this experiment) → endothelial cells): TGF-β2 with IL-1β induced the mesenchymal phenotype while IFN-γ alone most strongly induced MHC-II genes; the triple combination gave the highest RUNX1 and most profoundly induced genes associated with indirect T-cell activation (IL6, IL18BP, IL15, IL12A), producing a profile closely resembling the in vivo IMEC signature. The same treatment applied to human pericytes or fibroblasts failed to induce RUNX1, and RUNX1 induction was confirmed in primary mouse cardiac and human cardiac endothelial cells [Evidence: Functional perturbation (exogenous ligand combinations in vitro)]
CF057-INT-F05 (Endothelial IFN-γ signalling → infarct size and fibrosis; IMECs ↔ T cells (spatial)): Endothelial Ifngr1 deletion improved left ventricular systolic function 4 weeks after MI, decreased infarct size and significantly reduced cardiac fibrosis. IMECs mapped specifically to the border and infarct zones of mouse hearts at day 1, and in human MI data endothelial cells colocalized with smooth muscle cells, pericytes and pan-T/mature NK-T clusters, with higher endothelial–T-cell colocalization in the border zone [Evidence: Functional perturbation (receptor deletion) plus computational spatial deconvolution (human dataset reused, flagged)]
g.text: Myeloid IL-1β/TNF plus TGF-β2 and IFN-γ; endothelial IFNGR1 loss

g.title:
EC out-signalling expands in heart failure
CF004-INT-F01 (Endothelial cells (all subclusters; endocardial and angiogenic most affected) → all other cardiac cell types): Inferred number of interactions involving endothelial cells was increased in ICM relative to NF, most pronounced for endocardial and angiogenic endothelial subtypes [Evidence: Computational prediction]
CF004-INT-F02 (Endothelial subclusters (LAMA4, LAMB1, LAMC1 expressing) → many cardiac cell types): Little LAMININ-based signalling from endothelial cells in NF; markedly expanded in ICM, attributed by the authors to increased LAMA4, LAMB1 and LAMC1 in several endothelial subclusters [Evidence: Computational prediction]
CF004-INT-F03 (Endothelial cells → other cardiac cell types): Signalling assigned to CDH5, JAM, COLLAGEN and LAMININ categories was significantly increased from endothelial sources in ICM compared with NF [Evidence: Computational prediction]
CF004-INT-F04 (No sender–receiver pair assigned (spatial association only)): EC-lymphatic cells were increased in ICM and the CCL21+ cells observed were clustered within fibrotic regions of the tissue; EC-angiogenic (PECAM1+MYO1B+) cells were instead distributed in capillaries throughout the tissue [Evidence: Observational]
CF006-INT-F01 (Endocardial cells (DCM state Ecd2) → candidate receiver cardiomyocytes (not demonstrated)): Endocardial cells from DCM upregulated NRG1 and reduced NRG3, while donor endocardial cells expressed NRG3; DCM endocardial cells also upregulated BMP4/6, GDF6, SVEP1, ELN, CTGF, EDN1, CYR61 and downregulated SEMA3A, VEGF-C, WNT9B, EDNRB, IGFBP4/6 [Evidence: Observational]
CF006-INT-F06 (Vascular endothelial cells (artery, vein, capillary) → receiver not assigned): Vascular endothelial cells did not diversify into new states in DCM but showed global expression shifts, including increased VEGF-A/VEGF-C, APLNR, FGFR1 and SMAD3/6; venous cells were enriched for TGF-β, NGF and MAPK pathways in DCM; lymphatics had few differentially expressed genes [Evidence: Observational]
CF011-INT-F06 (Capillary-like immune-related endothelial cells (EC4_immune) → immune cells (receiver not demonstrated); FB3 fibroblasts as cytokine receivers): An endothelial population (EC4_immune) expressed antigen-presentation and immune-regulatory transcripts including CX3CL1, CCL2, IL6 and ICAM1; FB3 fibroblasts expressed low ECM genes but high cytokine receptors including OSMR and IL6ST, and an OSM-signalling fibroblast population was recovered separately in each chamber (aFB4, vFB3) [Evidence: Observational (expression only)]
g.text: EC out-signalling expands in heart failure

g.title:
Lymphatics clear macrophages from the infarct
CF078-INT-F02 (Cardiac macrophages (efferocytic, TIM4+CCR2− resident) → lymphatic endothelial cells): Sorted cardiac macrophages increased Vegfc after MI and showed a selective Vegfc signature compared with neutrophils and monocytes; macrophages with higher ingested cardiomyocyte antigen expressed more VEGFC, and TIM4+CCR2− resident macrophages had both higher efferocytic activity and higher VEGFC than recruited CCR2+ macrophages. CD68+ macrophages lay proximal to LYVE1+ lymphatics. Myeloid Cd36 deficiency reduced myocardial Vegfc, macrophage VEGFC and LYVE1+ lymphatic staining and reduced cardiac antigen accumulation in mediastinal lymph nodes; VEGFR3 inhibition reduced antigen uptake by cardiac and lymph node macrophages [Evidence: Observational (expression and localisation) plus functional perturbation (myeloid deletion, receptor inhibition)]
CF078-INT-F03 (Myeloid-derived VEGFC → cardiac lymphatics, remodelling and fibrosis): Myeloid Vegfc deletion reduced LYVE1+ lymphatics in the ischemic area at risk, reduced ejection fraction with pronounced left ventricular dilation, and increased scarring and fibrosis at 28 days, without a difference in acute infarct size or area at risk. Myeloid Vegfc gain of function improved post-MI ejection fraction, increased cardiac lymphatics and increased the frequency of macrophages with lower MHC-II. The same functional requirement was seen after ischemia/reperfusion [Evidence: Functional perturbation (cell-type-restricted deletion and overexpression)]
CF078-INT-F04 (Macrophage-derived VEGFC → macrophages (autocrine/paracrine) and the infarct immune environment): Myeloid Vegfc deficiency produced a dysregulated inflammatory signature with increased inflammation-associated genes and reduced inflammation-resolution and lymphatic-response genes, increased inflammatory polarization of cardiac macrophages (while earlier inflammation was unaffected), and fewer infarct-associated Tregs despite maintained lymph node levels. Vegfc-deficient macrophages had elevated Tnfa and reduced Arg1 in culture, and recombinant VEGFC reduced Tnfa, Il6 and Il12 in LPS-activated macrophages. Myeloid Cd36-deficient animals likewise retained more MHCIIhi inflammatory macrophages [Evidence: Functional perturbation (genetic deletion plus recombinant ligand)]
CF079-INT-F02 (Lymphatic endothelium → immune cells (clearance from the infarct)): CD68+ macrophages were closely associated with LYVE-1+ capillaries, most evidently at day 4. VEGF-C treatment reduced cardiac CD45+ leukocytes, CD11b+ myeloid cells, macrophages and dendritic cells at day 7 and increased CD68+ macrophage content in mediastinal lymph nodes, with no difference at days 1 and 4 before lymphatic sprouting. Apoptotic CD68+ cells were scarce in both groups (0–2 per section) and no proliferating lymph node macrophages were found, excluding in situ apoptosis or nodal proliferation as explanations [Evidence: Functional perturbation (pharmacological stimulation) with negative controls for alternative mechanisms]
CF079-INT-F03 (Cardiomyocyte debris → macrophages → mediastinal lymph nodes): After MI, tdTomato+ cardiomyocyte-derived particles were detected within CD68+ cells in mediastinal lymph nodes adjacent to PDPN+ lymphatic sinuses, and were rare in uninjured animals. Adoptively transferred CD68+GFP+ monocytes engrafted in the infarct and were subsequently detected in draining lymph nodes, but not in sham-operated animals [Evidence: Observational with a cell-tracking perturbation (adoptive transfer)]
CF079-INT-F04 (Lymphatic endothelial LYVE-1 → leukocyte docking and transit): Lyve1−/− mice had normal resident macrophage numbers at baseline, equivalent area at risk and a grossly normal lymphangiogenic response (comparable VEGFR-3 network, Vegfc, Ccl21, Prox1, Vegfr3 and Has2), but retained significantly more CD45+ leukocytes, myeloid cells, neutrophils, macrophages and dendritic cells in the heart with fewer CD68+ cells in lymph nodes, and no increase in apoptotic macrophages. Ejection fraction and stroke volume fell and end-systolic volume rose by day 21, with extensive collagen deposition and increased thick (type-I-like) fibre birefringence. VEGF-C treatment did not rescue trafficking in the mutants [Evidence: Functional perturbation (constitutive gene knockout) with a failed rescue as a specificity control]
g.text: Lymphatics clear macrophages from the infarct

g.title:
Vascular rarefaction without lasting EndMT
CF059-INT-F04 (Remote zone → infarct zone (pro-angiogenic); infarct zone → infarct zone (anti-angiogenic, pro-fibrotic, inflammatory)): Regional communication was strongest at day 3. Vegfa and Vegfb were sourced exclusively from the remote zone and acted on both infarct layers, as was Angpt1, while the infarct zone was the dominant source of thrombospondins and Angpt2 and of inflammatory and pro-fibrotic signals; Vegfa/Vegfb were downregulated within the infarct at all time points. ELISA showed an overall VEGF-A increase at day 7 with no difference between tissue proximal and distal to the infarct. Activated pericytes were best predicted to reside in the infarct layers at day 3 [Evidence: Computational prediction from spatial transcriptomics, with one protein-level measurement that did not confirm the regional gradient]
CF060-INT-F03 (Endothelial cells → mesenchymal lineage (tested, not supported); endothelial proliferative response): Cycling and DNA-replicating endothelial cells increased at 14 days and then fell below sham levels at 28 days, confirmed by Ki-67 quantification, with angiogenic-EC marker Apln enriched in fibrotic regions; endocardial and lymphatic endothelial cells decreased. Cdh5 fate-traced cells had far lower ECM gene expression than all fibroblast populations and pericytes, did not increase ECM expression substantially after TAC, showed no enrichment of a published endothelial-mesenchymal activation signature, and no fate-traced endothelial cell appeared within fibroblast clusters [Evidence: Observational with lineage tracing (negative result for endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition)]
g.text: Remote VEGFA/B vs infarct THBS1/ANGPT2 signals; Cdh5-traced
ECs stay low in ECM genes

g.title:
EV miR-24-3p keeps fibroblasts quiescent
CF066-INT-F01 (Cardiomyocytes (principal cellular source of miR-24-3p) → fibroblasts (candidate at this step)): miR-24-3p was the second most abundant miR in healthy human hearts, and its targets FURIN, CCND1 and SMAD4 showed no to low expression in fibroblasts from normal hearts but prominent expression in fibroblasts from infarcted hearts. In culture, cardiomyocytes expressed high, endothelial cells low and fibroblasts undetectable miR-24-3p. A miR-24-3p mimic downregulated FURIN, CCND1 and SMAD4 in fibroblasts (more pronounced with TGF-β1) without affecting non-target genes endoglin and vimentin, and decreased TGF-β1 secretion by activated fibroblasts [Evidence: Observational (expression, including reused datasets) plus functional perturbation (mimic) in human cells]
CF066-INT-F02 (Cardiomyocytes → cardiac fibroblasts): A miR-24-3p mimic reduced fibroblast proliferation, αSMA+ cell numbers, collagen-1 C-peptide and POSTN. In microtissues, transfecting only the cardiomyocytes with anti-miR-24-3p before assembly increased vimentin+/cTnT+ area ratio and collagen-1 C-peptide, while POSTN was unchanged; a miR-24-3p mimic in cardiomyocytes reversed TGF-β1-mediated FURIN, CCND1 and SMAD4 upregulation in microtissues [Evidence: Functional perturbation (cell-type-restricted antagomir within a defined co-culture)]
CF066-INT-F03 (Cardiomyocyte-derived EVs → cardiac fibroblasts): Cardiomyocyte EVs were enriched in miR-24-3p and prevented TGF-β1-induced fibroblast activation. Transfecting cardiomyocytes with anti-miR-24-3p halved EV miR-24-3p and abolished the inhibitory effect, as did transfecting the recipient fibroblasts with anti-miR-24-3p. EVs from GW4869-treated cardiomyocytes failed to inhibit fibroblast activation, and dynasore or heparin pretreatment of fibroblasts attenuated the EV effect; EV uptake was visualised with labelled EVs [Evidence: Functional perturbation (cargo depletion plus release and uptake inhibition)]
CF066-INT-F04 (Ischaemic cardiomyocytes → fibroblasts (loss of the protective signal)): Ischaemia-simulating conditions increased microtissue vimentin+/cTnT+ ratio, markedly reduced miR-24-3p and increased markers of cardiomyocyte stress without changing cardiomyocyte number; hypoxic human cardiac slices showed increased αSMA and reduced miR-24-3p. Cardiomyocytes under these conditions secreted more and larger EVs with lower miR-24-3p content that failed to prevent TGF-β1-mediated fibroblast activation, and the same cargo reduction occurred in EVs from ischaemic microtissues and hypoxic slices. Post-mortem MI hearts showed decreased miR-24-3p by RNAScope, and circulating EVs from STEMI patients had lower miR-24-3p than healthy subjects [Evidence: Functional perturbation (ischaemia simulation) plus observational human tissue and biofluid data]
g.text: Targets FURIN, CCND1 and SMAD4; the protective cargo is lost
