g.title:
Stressed, senescent myocytes are pro-fibrotic
CF017-INT-F02 (Cardiomyocytes (BAG3−/−) → fibroblasts (candidate; not demonstrated in co-culture)): BAG3−/− fibroblasts significantly increased TGFBR2 (including at the cell membrane) without upregulating TGF-β ligand, while knockout cardiomyocytes, but not knockout fibroblasts, increased TGF-β1 secretion; GSEA showed increased TGF-β pathway signature in BAG3−/− CFs, and THBS1, LOX, LOXL2, LOXL3 were increased [Evidence: Observational (expression/secretion) within a knockout model]
CF068-INT-F01 (Cardiomyocytes (senescent) → myocardium (remodelling and function)): Cardiomyocyte p16 deletion reduced p16+ and p21+ cardiomyocytes in the peri-infarct region (about fivefold and twofold respectively), improved ejection fraction with better preserved systolic volume, and significantly reduced scar size, without altering left ventricular mass or cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area. Telomere-associated foci rose equally in both genotypes after injury (about 40% of cardiomyocytes), and superoxide by DHE did not differ [Evidence: Functional perturbation (cardiomyocyte-restricted conditional deletion)]
CF068-INT-F02 (Senescent cardiomyocytes → surrounding non-cardiomyocyte cells (paracrine senescence)): Cardiomyocyte p16 deletion decreased several secreted proteins in the myocardium, with a significant reduction in IL-6 and trends for IFN-γ and G-CSF, and reduced p16-expressing and SA-β-galactosidase-positive interstitial cells in the myofibroblast-rich peri-infarct region [Evidence: Observational (whole-tissue cytokine measurement and interstitial cell counts) within a genetic perturbation]
CF069-INT-F01 (Cell-intrinsic in cardiomyocytes (upstream of intercellular signalling)): Isoproterenol increased cardiomyocyte NOX4 (strongly mitochondrial) and cellular and mitochondrial ROS in wild-type but not Nox4-deficient hearts, without changes in NOX1, NOX2, SOD1/2, catalase or mitochondrial mass. Cleaved caspase-1 and IL-18 rose in wild-type hearts and cardiomyocytes but not in Nox4-deficient ones, with NLRP3 expression itself unchanged, and tissue IL-18, IL-6, CCL2 and TNFα were higher in wild-type mice; GKT137831 reproduced the attenuation in cultured cardiomyocytes [Evidence: Functional perturbation (cell-type-specific genetic deletion and pharmacological inhibition)]
CF069-INT-F04 (Cardiomyocyte NOX4 → interstitial fibrosis and diastolic function): Interstitial collagen deposition increased in wild-type but was significantly lower in Nox4-deficient hearts, without measurable cardiomyocyte necrosis or apoptosis or changes in plasma LDH, so the collagen was not replacement fibrosis. Ejection fraction, end-diastolic volume and heart weight were unchanged, while wild-type mice developed increased E, decreased E′, increased E/E′, shortened deceleration time, higher end-diastolic pressure and EDPVR and altered dP/dtmin — all attenuated in Nox4-deficient mice. GKT137831 reduced mitochondrial ROS, CD11b+ cells, fibrosis and the diastolic abnormalities. Isovolumic relaxation time and tau were unchanged, which the authors state does not support altered cardiomyocyte relaxation [Evidence: Functional perturbation (genetic and pharmacological) with explicitly reported negative results]
g.text: BAG3−/− CM secrete TGF-β1; p16+ CM secrete IL-6; CM NOX4

g.title:
ZEB2 → TMSB4/PTMA promotes angiogenesis
CF026-INT-F02 (Epicardial cells → macrophages; cardiomyocytes → endothelial cells; fibroblasts and macrophages → many cell types): In unstressed hearts, fibroblasts and macrophages were key signalling hubs of the interstitial niche, with dendritic-like, epicardial and endocardial cells also forming extensive networks, while granulocytes, NK cells and lymphocytes were least interactive. Epicardial cells were the most enriched for Csf1, identifying them as the most macrophage-trophic population, and cardiomyocytes were the primary Vegfa producers; macrophage subsets showed distinct spatial distribution relative to the epicardium [Evidence: Computational prediction with supporting spatial observation]
CF071-INT-F01 (Injured cardiomyocytes (ZEB2 induction)): Cardiomyocytes from infarcted hearts clustered separately from sham, and ZEB2 was identified among 11 transcription factors enriched in injured cardiomyocytes. ZEB2 protein was detected in injured cardiomyocytes flanking the infarct and also in macrophages and other immune cells; ZEB2 was confirmed in a portion of cardiomyocytes from patients with ischemic heart disease but not detected in control human heart. Zeb2 expression peaked 3–7 days after MI [Evidence: Observational (single-cell transcriptomics and protein localisation)]
CF071-INT-F02 (Cardiomyocyte ZEB2 → coronary vasculature and infarct healing): Cardiomyocyte Zeb2 deletion worsened fractional shortening, increased infarct size, produced a dilated infarct region and remote-zone cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, decreased BCL-XL, and reduced Pecam1 and Vegf expression with lower PECAM1+ vessel area in remote and border zones (a vascular difference was already present after sham). Bulk RNA-seq showed downregulation of focal adhesion, PI3K-Akt and actin cytoskeleton pathways, indicating effects beyond cardiomyocytes. Cardiomyocyte-specific ZEB2 overexpression had the opposite effects, improving function, reducing infarct size and fibrosis, increasing PECAM1 and BCL-XL, and reducing remote cardiomyocyte hypertrophy [Evidence: Functional perturbation (cell-type-specific deletion and overexpression)]
CF071-INT-F03 (Cardiomyocytes → endothelial cells (and fibroblasts)): Conditioned medium from ZEB2-manipulated cardiomyocytes did not alter the cardiomyocyte fraction but changed ECM/fibrotic and endothelial genes in non-cardiomyocytes; the smaller-protein fraction from ZEB2-overexpressing cardiomyocytes increased endothelial migration and angiogenesis-related gene expression. Mass spectrometry plus RNA-seq filtering identified 11 candidates, of which Tmsb4 and Ptma (with Rack1 and Dynll1) were significantly downregulated in Zeb2 cKO hearts and confirmed at protein level. Conditioned medium from cardiomyocytes overexpressing ZEB2, TMSB4 or PTMA increased endothelial migration with no additive effect; ZEB2 knockdown reduced migration, sprouting and EdU incorporation, and this was rescued by TMSB4 or PTMA overexpression. Knocking down TMSB4 or PTMA individually did not affect sprouting, but knocking down both reproduced the ZEB2 knockdown effect [Evidence: Functional perturbation (sender-side manipulation with rescue, in vitro)]
CF071-INT-F04 (Therapeutically delivered cardiomyocyte ZEB2 → endothelium): Intracardiac AAV9-Zeb2 increased ZEB2 at both time points, improved fractional shortening and left ventricular dimensions after MI, increased Tmsb4 and Ptma, increased Pecam1 and Vegf expression and PECAM1+ area, produced a trend toward elevated BCL-XL at 28 days, and reduced remote-zone cardiomyocyte size [Evidence: Functional perturbation (therapeutic gene delivery)]

g.data-finding-ids: CF053-INT-F01 CF053-INT-F02 CF053-INT-F03 CF053-INT-F04 CF053-INT-F05 CF053-INT-F06 CF053-INT-F07 CF069-INT-F02 CF069-INT-F03
g.title:
Exophers are cleared by resident MΦ via MERTK
CF053-INT-F01 (Cardiac-resident macrophages ↔ cardiomyocytes): Resident macrophages were ubiquitously distributed in the myocardium and each cardiomyocyte was surrounded on average by five macrophages, with each macrophage interacting with up to five cardiomyocytes through cellular processes; comparable structures and macrophages were found in human myocardium [Evidence: Observational (imaging)]
CF053-INT-F02 (Cardiomyocytes → resident macrophages (dominant); endothelial cells → macrophages (lesser); circulating leukocytes → macrophages): Resident macrophages, but not cardiac monocytes, took up abundant fluorescent material from cardiomyocytes and circulating cells and less from endothelial cells; cardiomyocyte-derived particles ("cardiac exophers", mean diameter ~3.5 µm) were abundant in healthy myocardium, about 40% in contact with or inside macrophages, with a distribution not explained by chance; horizontal transfer of tdTomato mRNA was ruled out. Exopher proteome was massively enriched for mitochondrial proteins with reduction of other compartments and of OPA1, FIS1, CYTC and AIFM1 [Evidence: Observational with genetic source-labelling controls]
CF053-INT-F03 (Cardiomyocytes → resident macrophages): Macrophages sorted from the heart incorporated parenchyma-derived mtDNA at much higher rates than macrophages from other tissues (only skeletal muscle showed low transfer); cardiomyocyte-restricted mt-Keima accumulated inside CD68+ macrophages, mostly in LAMP1+ acidic compartments, and both mt-Keima signal and donor mtDNA were lost after 2–3 days of macrophage culture, indicating degradation [Evidence: Observational with genetic tracing of cargo origin]
CF053-INT-F04 (Cardiomyocyte autophagy machinery → exopher production → macrophage uptake): Most exophers contained LC3 puncta; rapamycin increased exopher number and increased transfer of cardiomyocyte-derived fluorescence and mt-Keima to macrophages, whereas cardiomyocyte-specific Atg7 hemizygous deletion dramatically reduced exopher numbers and reduced transfer [Evidence: Functional perturbation (pharmacological and genetic, sender side)]
CF053-INT-F05 (Resident macrophages → cardiomyocytes (clearance-dependent support)): Macrophage depletion doubled exopher content after 2 days and led to marked accumulation of free extracellular mitochondria; longer depletion produced progressive decline and near absence of exophers by 3 weeks with complete block of cardiomyocyte autophagy flux (not present at 2 days), inflammasome activation, increased mitochondrial number with enlarged area and reduced cristae density, reduced ATP production, a shift to glucose use, and diastolic and systolic dysfunction that was restored when macrophages repopulated the heart. NLRP3 inhibition with MCC950 rescued the autophagic block and partially restored exopher formation. Liver mitochondrial ATP and content were unaffected despite depletion in that organ [Evidence: Functional perturbation (depletion and pharmacological rescue)]
CF053-INT-F06 (Cardiomyocyte-derived exophers → macrophages (receptor-dependent uptake)): Exophers exposed phosphatidylserine and annexin V patches were distributed closer to macrophages than random dots; transfer of cardiomyocyte-derived mt-Keima into macrophages was severely compromised in Mertk−/− mice despite higher macrophage numbers, with accumulation of free extracellular mitochondria, inflammasome activation, blunted autophagy, increased mitochondrial content with reduced cristae density, diminished ATP production in older mice, reduced E/A ratio and increased 18F-FDG uptake [Evidence: Functional perturbation (germline receptor deletion)]
CF053-INT-F07 (Stressed cardiomyocytes → resident macrophages): Isoproterenol reduced cardiomyocyte mitochondrial quality and increased exopher numbers and transfer of cardiomyocyte material and mt-Keima to macrophages; protection from mitochondrial damage in Oma1−/− mice blunted the isoproterenol-induced transfer. After MI, cardiomyocyte-derived particles sharing exopher morphology and mitochondrial content accumulated at the periphery of the infarct, but macrophage analyses were not possible there because of massive inflammatory macrophage infiltration into regions devoid of cardiomyocytes. Macrophage depletion worsened isoproterenol-induced dysfunction and caused early mortality after reperfusion [Evidence: Functional perturbation plus observational (ischaemic context)]
CF069-INT-F02 (Cardiomyocytes (via NOX4-dependent inflammation) → cardiac macrophage populations): Wild-type hearts had more CD11b+ and CD68+ macrophages 3 days after isoproterenol than Nox4-deficient hearts, with no mobilization of peripheral Ly6Chi monocytes in either genotype. t-SNE identified 8 clusters: none contained classical recruited pro-inflammatory monocyte-derived macrophages; embryonic-derived resident (CCR2−MHCII+) clusters 2 and 3, expressing TGFβ and IL6 (with MKI67 or LY6C/LGALS3), were enriched in wild-type and depleted in Nox4-deficient hearts, whereas resident repair clusters 4–6 (CCR2−MHCIIloCX3CR1lo) were enriched in Nox4-deficient and depleted in wild-type hearts [Evidence: Observational (high-dimensional cytometry) within a genetic perturbation]
CF069-INT-F03 (Macrophages (pro-fibrotic resident subsets) → cardiac fibroblasts): The FAP+ fibroblast proportion did not differ by genotype, but 7 clusters shifted after isoproterenol: proliferative clusters were enriched in both genotypes, an anchored collagen-secreting myofibroblast cluster was relatively depleted in both, and a protomyofibroblast cluster with high COL1A1 and low CD90 was enriched in wild-type but depleted in Nox4-deficient hearts. POSTN+ non-myocytes increased 6.5-fold in wild-type hearts at 7 days and were significantly less abundant in Nox4-deficient hearts, with a 3-fold higher ACTA2+ non-myocyte fraction in wild-type at 3 days [Evidence: Observational (cytometry and histology) within a genetic perturbation]

g.data-finding-ids: CF052-INT-F04 CF052-INT-F05 CF052-INT-F07 CF087-INT-F04 CF087-INT-F05 CF087-INT-F07
g.title:
Physical coupling with macrophages
CF052-INT-F04 (CCR2− resident macrophages ↔ cardiomyocytes): CCR2− macrophages extended processes that physically contacted cardiomyocytes and formed stable contacts over 90 minutes, with greater projection length in failing hearts; CCR2+ macrophages extended processes into the interstitium without contacting cardiomyocytes. FAK was frequently present at macrophage–cardiomyocyte contacts and no desmosome, adherens, tight or gap junction densities were observed. In co-culture, paxillin localised to BMDM–HL-1 contacts and antibodies blocking either β1- or β2-integrin disrupted the interaction, with β1 blockade also abolishing paxillin staining at contact sites [Evidence: Functional perturbation in vitro plus observational in vivo imaging]
CF052-INT-F05 (Mechanical stretch (not a cell sender) → macrophages; macrophages → downstream angiogenic/remodelling readouts): Cyclic stretch increased macrophage Igf1, Hbegf and Cyr61, and this was blocked by the TRPV4 inhibitor; Myd88 or Trif deletion had no effect, and LPS or polyIC did not induce these genes nor did stretch induce inflammatory cytokines. TRPV4 inhibition in Tnnt2DK210/DK210 mice reduced macrophage IGF1 (frequency and intensity), while the agonist increased it; 2-week TRPV4 inhibition left trabecular myocardium persistent, attenuated LV dilation without changing ejection fraction, and markedly reduced coronary microvascular density and large coronary artery complexity in mutants without affecting control microvascular density [Evidence: Functional perturbation (pharmacological and genetic)]
CF052-INT-F07 (CCR2− resident macrophages → cardiomyocyte mitochondria; → cardiac conduction): No differences in mitochondrial respiration were detected across experimental groups, and no significant differences in RR, PR or QRS intervals were observed, with QT prolongation similar in mutants with and without depletion; MMP9 activity was negligible in control and Tnnt2DK210/DK210 hearts. Both CCR2− and CCR2+ macrophages were located within the atrioventricular node [Evidence: Functional perturbation with negative results]
CF087-INT-F04 (TRMPs ↔ cardiomyocytes): 85.2% of TRMPs showed at least two CX43 puncta at contacts with adjacent cardiomyocytes and AREG was significantly upregulated in assembloids; mCherry+ TRMPs showed calcium transients and action potentials synchronized with neighbouring cardiomyocytes, and expressed calcium and potassium channel transcripts (CACNA1F, KCNA3, KCNJ10, KCNMA1, KCNN4, TRPA1, TRPC2, TRPM2, TRPV2, TRPV4). TRMP APD30, APD50 and APD90 were prolonged relative to cardiomyocytes [Evidence: Observational (imaging) with expression support; no uncoupling perturbation]
CF087-INT-F05 (Apoptotic/dying cells → TRMPs): Untreated assembloids had significantly more ApoTracker+ TRMPs than organoids or inhibitor-treated assembloids; phagocytosis pathways were enriched in assembloids; CALR colocalized preferentially with CD45+ TRMP regions and MERTK was significantly higher in CD45+ TRMPs than other cell types [Evidence: Functional perturbation (pharmacological inhibition)]
CF087-INT-F07 (TRMPs → ventricular cardiomyocytes): Assembloids showed larger contraction amplitudes, shorter sarcomere lengths consistent with contracted cardiomyocytes, higher MYL3 expression and upregulated myogenesis genes relative to organoids [Evidence: Observational (comparison of reconstituted vs macrophage-free tissue)]
